My neighborhood loves Halloween. Everyone sits on their doorstep, with a cocktail, and hands out candy and the occasional trick. Sometimes they dress up as whatever the current fad is with the kids. This year, I expect to see a lot of Minecraft characters and probably a few horse heads.

Every year we get out our old Radio Flyer and pack in the tricks. Party string - glow sticks - little ghosts - plastic spiders - Beer. We only spray the people we know, of course, and we usually end up giving it away so the kids can play tricks on each other. Cheap and fun and it's biodegradable. yay, environmental goodness.

There's several retired PD and a few active duties so the parents and grandparents wandering the streets with a margarita glass or a bottle of home brew isn't an issue. Lots of families have settled close together so there's always an impromptu gathering and it seems like everyone is welcome to attend.

There's one lady who dresses up like Bette Davis, complete with a tight dress and cigarette in a long holder. Every year! She tells me it's the only way she can smoke without anyone giving her a lecture. She's pushing 90. She's lovely.

I make up a special packet of treats for my neighbors kids. They're past the age of trick or treating but they still get a treat. We just drop it off when we go over for my little one. It's always appreciated, plus I consider it extra protection against minor teenager vandalism. Probably won't happen but it doesn't hurt!

We give the other treaters random dollar store stuff, with a special extra bag thrown in for mom and dad. This year, the parents got gum and pretzels, both on sale at the dollar store. The kids got some plastic toys and some candy.

The bags were 25 for a dollar.
The coins were 25 for a dollar.
The plastic critters were 100 for a dollar.
Gum and lollies were 50 for a dollar.
Pixie sticks were 50 for a dollar.
Stickers were 15 for a dollar.
And the marbles were 100 for a dollar.

So in total we spent about 10 bucks on Halloween crap and about an hour in time. We watched the Fellowship while we separated all the stuff and put them in bags. A fun time.

Holidays are fun. Hope you enjoy yours!
